payload.task_text:
I manage the infrastructure team and need a full availability report for our three critical services. The raw monitoring data is in service_status_log.json in the workspace. This file contains 504 hourly status checks covering three services over seven days, from February 27 through March 5, 2026. Each entry has a timestamp, service_name, status (which is one of up, down, or degraded), response_time_ms, and error_message (null when the service is up).

Please analyze this data and create an Excel file called Service_Availability_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Availability Summary" and have the following columns: Service_Name, Total_Checks, Up_Count, Down_Count, Degraded_Count, Uptime_Pct, and Avg_Response_Time_Ms. Uptime_Pct should be calculated as the number of up checks divided by total checks times 100, rounded to one decimal place. Avg_Response_Time_Ms should be rounded to two decimal places. There should be one row per service, so three rows total.

The second sheet should be called "Incidents" and list every continuous period where a service was in a down or degraded state. The columns should be Service_Name, Start_Time, End_Time, Duration_Minutes, Status, and Error_Message. A new incident row should be created each time a service transitions from up to down or degraded, and the incident ends when the service returns to up. Duration_Minutes should reflect how many minutes the incident lasted based on the timestamps.

Next, create a page in the knowledge base titled "Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026" that summarizes the findings. The page should describe the overall availability of each service, highlight any services with downtime or degraded performance, and note the specific incident windows.

For each service that experienced any downtime during the monitoring period, create a calendar event on the shared team calendar on March 7, 2026 from 10:00 to 10:30. Title the event "Incident Review: [Service_Name]" where you replace [Service_Name] with the actual service name. In the event description, include a brief summary of the downtime incidents for that service.

Finally, send an email from monitoring@company.com to devops-team@company.com with the subject "Service Availability Report - Week of Feb 27" that lists each service whose uptime was below 99 percent, along with their actual uptime percentage and a note about the incidents observed.

Note on existing workspace content: the knowledge base and shared calendar may contain pre-existing unrelated content such as onboarding checklists, company handbook entries, weekly all-hands, department training sessions, or Q1 budget review events. Leave those items in place. Do not delete, rename, or merge them into your incident review artifacts. Only create new pages, events, and emails for the monitoring report work described above.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one sub-agent wave because the 504-row incident scan is the only data-heavy branch.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The coder sub-agent is the sole owner of `Service_Availability_Report.xlsx`. Read all 504 rows from `service_status_log.json`, sort within each of the three services, compute the exact summary metrics, and collapse each maximal consecutive down/degraded run into one incident ending at the return-to-up timestamp or observation-window boundary. Create the exact two-sheet workbook and read it back once. Return the workbook path plus a compact structured handoff containing all three summary rows and every incident row; do not create another JSON file and do not touch Notion, Calendar, or email.

After Wave 1, the main agent checks the 504-row and three-service controls once. From the returned compact handoff, it directly creates or updates exactly one page titled `Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026` and natively parallelizes exact event lookups/creates for services with at least one down check at 2026-03-07 10:00–10:30 using the runtime calendar default. After one page/event read-back, send exactly one email from `monitoring@company.com` to `devops-team@company.com` with subject `Service Availability Report - Week of Feb 27`, listing only services below 99 percent. Preserve unrelated objects and do not dispatch another wave.

You are creating a single Notion page. This is an authorized external write via the granted Notion MCP tools only.

## Context
I have finished analyzing a service monitoring dataset (504 hourly status checks, 3 services, 2026-02-27 00:00 UTC through 2026-03-05 23:00 UTC, i.e. 168 checks per service). I need the findings published as a page in the shared knowledge base. The workspace already contains unrelated top-level pages ("Onboarding Checklist", "Company Handbook", "Q1 OKR Draft") — DO NOT modify, delete, rename, or merge those. Only create one new page.

## Task
1. Create a new Notion page titled exactly: `Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026`
2. Create it as a workspace-level / top-level page (sibling of "Onboarding Checklist", "Company Handbook", "Q1 OKR Draft"). If workspace-level creation is rejected, fall back to creating it under the "Company Handbook" page as a child, and tell me which parent you used.
3. Add the page body content described below.
4. Report back: the new page ID, the page URL, which parent was used, and a verbatim copy of any tool error you hit.

## Page body content to add
- Intro paragraph: "Availability report for our three critical services, based on hourly status checks between 2026-02-27 00:00 UTC and 2026-03-05 23:00 UTC (7 days, 504 checks total = 168 checks per service). Source data: service_status_log.json. Full detail, including the complete incident log, is in Service_Availability_Report.xlsx."
- Heading "Overall Availability", plus a short note: "Uptime is calculated as the number of 'up' checks divided by total checks. Degraded checks are not counted as uptime. Avg Response Time is the mean response time in milliseconds across all checks, including checks taken while the service was down or degraded."
- A table with 7 columns and 4 rows (header + 3 data rows):
  Header: Service | Total Checks | Up | Down | Degraded | Uptime % | Avg Response Time (ms)
  Row 1: API Gateway | 168 | 164 | 4 | 0 | 97.6% | 312.09
  Row 2: Auth Service | 168 | 166 | 0 | 2 | 98.8% | 87.72
  Row 3: Database | 168 | 168 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% | 35.08
- Heading "Services With Downtime or Degraded Performance"
  - Sub-heading "API Gateway - hard downtime (worst performer)" and a paragraph: "The API Gateway was the only service that actually went down. It recorded 4 'down' checks out of 168, giving 97.6% uptime - the lowest of the three services and the only one to break the 99% availability target. Its average response time of 312.09 ms is also by far the highest of the three, driven by the very high response times observed during the outages (7,584-9,956 ms). Two separate outage windows occurred, each lasting 2 hours, for a combined 240 minutes of downtime."
  - Sub-heading "Auth Service - degraded performance" and a paragraph: "The Auth Service never went fully down, but it ran in a degraded state for 2 hourly checks, giving 98.8% uptime - just below the 99% target. Average response time was 87.72 ms, elevated by the 998 ms and 1,525 ms response times seen during the degraded window. A single 2-hour degraded-performance window was recorded."
  - Sub-heading "Database - fully healthy" and a paragraph: "The Database had a clean week: 168 of 168 checks 'up' (100.0% uptime), no down or degraded checks, and the lowest average response time of the three services at 35.08 ms."
- Heading "Specific Incident Windows" with a note: "Three incidents were recorded in total. Each began at the first non-'up' check and ended when the next hourly check reported the service back 'up'. A new incident row is generated only on a transition from 'up' to 'down'/'degraded'." Then a numbered list:
  1. "Incident 1 - API Gateway (down): 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC to 2026-03-01 04:00 UTC (120 minutes). Error: \"Connection timeout - upstream server not responding\"."
  2. "Incident 2 - Auth Service (degraded): 2026-03-02 08:00 UTC to 2026-03-02 10:00 UTC (120 minutes). Error: \"High latency detected on authentication requests\"."
  3. "Incident 3 - API Gateway (down): 2026-03-04 00:00 UTC to 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC (120 minutes). Error: \"502 Bad Gateway - backend service unavailable\"."
- Heading "Key Takeaways" with a bulleted list:
  - "2 of 3 services fell below the 99% uptime threshold: API Gateway (97.6%) and Auth Service (98.8%)."
  - "API Gateway is the only service with true downtime (2 outages, 240 minutes total) and needs an incident review."
  - "Auth Service experienced degraded latency only (never a full outage); its average response time of 87.72 ms is still reasonable, but the degraded window should be investigated."
  - "Database had a clean week: 100% uptime, 0 incidents and the lowest average response time (35.08 ms)."
  - "Recommended follow-up: an \"Incident Review: API Gateway\" meeting has been scheduled for 2026-03-07 10:00-10:30, and the sub-99% services have been flagged to devops-team@company.com."

## Important technical note
If the `mcp__notion__API-post-page` call fails with an error like `Invalid args for tool ... /parent must be object ... /properties must be object`, that means the `parent` and `properties` arguments were not transmitted as JSON objects. In that case, try these variations in order and report exactly which one worked:
  (a) Pass `parent` as `{"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}` and `properties` as `{"title": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "Service Monitoring Dashboard - March 2026"}}]}}` in a single API-post-page call together with the `children` array.
  (b) Create the page with just `parent` and `properties` (no children), then use `mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children` on the returned page ID to append the body content.
  (c) Use a `page_id` parent referencing the existing "Company Handbook" page (id 30ea211c-9408-435b-8686-79f04618b7d1).
Do not give up after one attempt — try all variations, and if every one fails, report the exact error text for each.

Do not touch the existing pages other than potentially using "Company Handbook" as a parent. Do not create any other pages, databases, comments, or events.
Create Notion monitoring page
